requirement:
`habeas coverage-check` MUST check saved execution coverage against
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.threshold` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.functions`, returning success only when
every applicable obligation is satisfied or has accepted exception evidence
under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`. The command MUST NOT
build the project, execute tests, collect coverage, or invoke an assessment model.
rationale:
**Scope.** `requirements.test-coverage.check` is an umbrella requirement. Its own obligations are:
- `habeas coverage-check` checks saved coverage against the threshold and function policies.
- It succeeds only when every applicable obligation is satisfied or has accepted exception evidence.
- It MUST NOT build, run tests, collect coverage, or invoke an assessment model.

The details of threshold, function scope and exceptions belong to the cited requirements `check.threshold`, `check.functions` and `check.exceptions`. Those have their own `{test}` references, mostly in `src/execution_coverage/check.rs#mod[tests]`, and I did not reassess them.

**Mapping obligations to tests**
- **Success and failure outcome of the command.** `tests/execution_coverage.rs#fn[full_test_flow_checks_real_function_counters_after_all_tests]` runs the full flow on a fixture with sync, async and integration tests.
  - It asserts that `habeas test` and the standalone `saved_check` (`habeas coverage-check`) both succeed and print "Coverage check passed".
  - It then adds an outer function containing a nested function and a closure. It asserts that the flow fails, that stdout names `#fn[outer]/fn[hidden]: zero execution`, and that it does not name `#fn[outer]: zero execution`. This applies `check.functions`, including its nested-function and closure rule, in the command's own case.
  - It asserts that the standalone check now fails with "Coverage check failed". It also asserts that the run outcome stays `success` (the policy caused the failure) and that the retained evidence is unchanged.
- **No model.** `model_tripwire` writes a `habeas.toml` pointing at a local listener and counts requests. The same test asserts the count is 0 after both the flow and the standalone `saved_check` runs, so `coverage-check` cannot have invoked a model.
- **No build, test execution or collection.** `tests/execution_coverage.rs#fn[book_rendering_preserves_retained_coverage_and_never_launches_tests]` captures coverage, then runs `coverage-check` with a `cargo` wrapper that allows only `metadata` and a test body that writes a marker file.
  - It asserts that the wrapper's forbidden-command log is absent (nothing but `metadata` ran).
  - It asserts that the marker file is absent (no test ran).
  - It asserts that the captured coverage files are byte-identical afterwards.
  - It asserts a non-zero exit with the "File execution coverage" report for filtered coverage that leaves unmeasured functions.
- **Exit-code mapping.** `src/main.rs#fn[main]` maps `report.passed` to the process exit code, and the two tests above check both the 0 and non-zero outcomes through the real binary.
- **Threshold and exception applicability.** The verdict logic for exact per-file thresholds, accepted file and function exceptions, stale or missing explanations, unmeasured files, and the rule that exceptions never transfer is tested in `check.rs#mod[tests]`. Examples are `accepted_file_and_function_explanations_remain_separate_from_execution`, `exact_per_file_threshold_and_partial_functions` and `missing_and_stale_explanations_fail_the_report`. Those tests carry `{test}` references to the refining requirements. `check_in` and `check` are thin wrappers over this logic, and the exit-code mapping is exercised both ways at the CLI level.

**Gaps considered.** The command-level tests do not end-to-end exercise a threshold failure or an accepted-exception success. The report-level tests cover those cases, and the CLI step between report and exit code is unconditional apart from the passed flag, which both integration tests exercise. Those report-level unit tests are not marked `{test}` for `check` itself, only for the refining requirements. Because the cited requirements' tests are not reassessed here, I treat this as covered rather than as an adequacy gap.

The reviewed tests enforce every obligation the subject states itself, so I found no unacknowledged gap.

text: :::{req} check
`habeas coverage-check` MUST check saved execution coverage against
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.threshold` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.functions`, returning success only when
every applicable obligation is satisfied or has accepted exception evidence
under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`. The command MUST NOT
build the project, execute tests, collect coverage, or invoke an assessment model.
:::{req} check.threshold
Each first-party Rust file under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage` MUST have at least 80%
execution coverage of its instrumented lines, or current accepted exception
evidence explaining why the file falls below that target under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`. Counts MUST use the
file-and-line union rule of {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.summary`;
a line counts as executed when any eligible test process or its associated
child processes has a positive execution count for it.
The check MUST use the combined selection and freshness rules of
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`, restricted to the active
build configuration. It MUST compare exact counts rather than rounded displayed
percentages, average file percentages, or impose an 80% target within each
function. A file whose executable code is not measured MUST require exception
evidence rather than pass with a fabricated percentage. A file established to
contain no executable coverage obligations MUST be reported as such and MUST
NOT require a threshold exception.
Absence of recorded instrumented lines alone MUST NOT establish that a file
contains no executable coverage obligations.
:::{req} check.functions
Every function under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.scope` without
recorded execution attributable to it MUST have current accepted exception
evidence under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`, even when
its containing file meets the target of
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.threshold`.
Execution attributable only to another function, including a nested function
or closure, MUST NOT establish coverage of the enclosing function merely
because their source locations overlap. Having no recorded lines alone MUST
NOT establish that a function has no executable coverage obligations.
:::{req} check.exceptions
An unmet file threshold or an unexecuted or not-measured function MAY satisfy
the coverage policy only
through current, accepted, independently assessed evidence explaining why its
coverage is incomplete. An exception MUST be attached to the source file or
function whose incomplete coverage it justifies. A file-threshold exception
MUST NOT automatically excuse untested functions.
An exception MUST NOT excuse another source item's incomplete coverage.
Changes to the source item, justification, or other inputs
of its citation review MUST invalidate the affected exception under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`.
A source comment or unassessed justification alone MUST NOT count as accepted
exception evidence. Function and gap identities MUST remain portable between
equivalent local and CI checkouts rather than depend on checkout paths,
run identifiers, timestamps, or process identifiers.
